Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our discussion I attached a light SOW draft and a simple uplift model that shows how a quarterly top-up would be applied if Aperture exceeds the committed reserved capacity. Key points:

- Base reserved capacity stays unchanged for the year.
- Quarterly uplift kicks in once monthly avg consumption > 110% of committed baseline for that quarter.
- Uplift pricing uses a hybrid band: 60% of uplift at committed rate, 40% at overage rate (discounted compared to pay-as-you-go).
- Co-term: If you add capacity mid-year we can annualize the uplift to co-term with the existing contract; that appears in the spreadsheet as a simple proration.

I kept the wording intentionally short — if you want a one-line for procurement that frames this as a "quarterly smoothing top-up with optional annualize-to-coterm" I can add it.

Next steps: Can you confirm whether procurement needs PO timing (this month vs. next quarter) and whether legal wants redlines on the SOW before we lock pricing? If procurement needs a fixed invoice cadence we can work with Lauren to map the billing split.

Sara — thanks, great questions. Looping in Lauren (billing/ops) and Ben (sales lead) so we can answer precisely. Quick answers inline below, then Lauren will confirm invoice mechanics and Ben will confirm co-term discount behavior.

> 1) Example month for 140% of baseline

See first tab in the attached spreadsheet for a worked example: baseline = 1M tokens/month; observed = 1.4M tokens in May (140%). Under the hybrid band the uplift 0.4M is split: 60% (0.24M) billed at committed unit price (same as baseline), 40% (0.16M) billed at uplift rate = 0.65 * PAYG_RATE (reflects discount). Total invoice line items: base reserved line (1.0M at committed rate), uplift line A (0.24M at committed rate), uplift line B (0.16M at uplift rate).

> 2) Quarterly vs monthly billing

Lauren: can you confirm whether retrospective quarterly settlement (invoice following quarter for last quarter's uplift) is supported, and any constraints (e.g., max 90-day invoice window)?

> 3) Co-term behavior

Ben: short answer — when a customer annualizes a mid-year add, we offer two options: (A) true-up/prorate the remainder of the year at the committed rate (no additional discount), or (B) convert additional capacity into a committed add with a stepped discount tier depending on total annual committed size. Option B requires approval for material discounts; Ben can advise typical thresholds.

I also attached a one-page summary that procurement can use (first page of the SOW Word doc). If procurement wants a dedicated "PO cadence" clause we can add a short paragraph.

Hi Sara — copying final ops details so procurement/finance have what they need.

Invoice mechanics (ops answer):
- We support both monthly and quarterly billing cadences.
- If you elect quarterly retrospective settlement, uplift overage for QN will be calculated at quarter close and invoiced one cycle after (i.e., invoice dated within 30 days after quarter end). We do not invoice mid-quarter for retrospective quarterly settlement.
- For monthly billing we invoice overage on the next monthly invoice (standard net-30).

Line item representation: we will create explicit uplift line items with description "Quarterly uplift — hybrid band" and include the meter (tokens) and the split math. This is exportable as CSV for your GL.

Co-term/pricing:
- Option A (prorated annualize): committed rate holds; new annualized volume becomes part of your committed baseline but pricing per unit remains the committed rate.
- Option B (commit + discount): if you choose to convert additional capacity into a new committed tier we evaluate the total annual commitment and apply tiered discounts. Example: an incremental 50% increase of annual commitment typically qualifies for a 5–8% blended discount on the incremental units (requires commercial approval).

Operational notes:
- We cap retrospective invoices to a 90-day lookback per our billing policy.
- For audit/GL purposes we can provide a CSV monthly breakout and a single consolidated quarterly invoice when requested.

Next steps:
1) Sara/procurement to confirm billing cadence preference (monthly vs quarterly retrospective).
2) If co-term is desired, confirm whether Aperture prefers Option A (simple proration) or Option B (commit + discount) so Ben and I can prepare a final pricing sheet and an amended SOW.

If procurement needs me to present a one-slide summary to leadership I can join the Nov 12 meeting.
